title: Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing
summary: Event-driven architectures communicate via events. CQRS separates write and read models. Event sourcing stores state as an append-only event log. Powerful patterns — easy to overcomplicate.

sections.title: Event-driven integration
paragraphs: Services publish facts about what happened. Consumers update their own state. Loose coupling improves autonomy; debugging becomes distributed.

sections.title: CQRS
paragraphs: Writes optimize for invariants; reads optimize for queries via projections. Eventual consistency between sides is normal — design UX for it.

sections.title: Event sourcing
paragraphs: State = fold(events). Auditing and replay shine; schema evolution and snapshots become mandatory ops. Not every domain wants this complexity.

sections.title: When not to
paragraphs: CRUD with modest scale often needs a modular monolith first. Introduce events at real integration boundaries.

deepDive.title: Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing — Operations
paragraphs: Operating Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, Event-Driven, CQRS & Event Sourcing intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

keyTakeaways: Events decouple at a cost of complexity
CQRS/ES need rebuild and versioning discipline
whyItMatters: These patterns dominate modern service design discussions; misuse creates distributed monoliths of events.
reflectionQuestions: Where do you need rebuildable audit history vs simple CRUD?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
